title: Newton's method and an area
subject: maths
statement: Let f(x) = x^3 - 2x - {c}. (a) Use Newton's method from x0 = {x0} to find a root of f to 4 decimal places. (b) Find the area between the curve, the x-axis and the lines x = {a} and x = {b}. (c) Estimate the same area with the trapezium rule using {n} strips.

parts.hint: x(n+1) = x(n) - f(x(n)) / f'(x(n)). What is f'(x)?

steps.say: First differentiate: f dash of x is three x squared minus two.
From x nought, follow the tangent down to the x axis.
Repeat: each tangent lands closer to the root.

parts.hint: Integrate f from a to b.

steps.say: The area is the integral of f from a to b.

parts.hint: h = (b - a)/n, then h/2 times (first + 2 times the middle ones + last).

steps.say: Each strip is b minus a over n wide.
Add the trapezia: the ends once, the middle heights twice.

summary: Newton's method follows tangents to the axis
The trapezium rule overestimates a curve that bends upwards
